title: Likes and free time: mögen, gern, lieber, am liebsten (Was magst du?)
summary: Say what you like, what you prefer and what you like most, about food, drinks and your free time, and how often you do things.
goals: Say what you like: Ich mag ... and Ich ... gern
Say what you prefer and like most: lieber, am liebsten
Talk about your hobbies and how often you do them

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 11: Eating and leisure (Ich mag (nicht)!, Was macht dir Spaß?)

points: [[mögen]] (to like) can work like a modal verb: conjugated second (first in a yes/no question), the other verb at the end: [[Was magst du essen?]]
Usually it stands alone with a thing: [[Ich mag Pizza.]]
With an activity you'll hear [[Ich mag tanzen.]], but [[Ich tanze gern.]] is more common.
Conjugation: [[ich mag]], [[du magst]], [[er mag]], [[wir mögen]], [[ihr mögt]], [[sie mögen]]. The ich form changes its vowel; er/sie/es is the same as ich.

phrases.en: What do you like to eat?

points: Hobbies at home: [[fernsehen]], [[lesen]], [[kochen]], [[malen]] (paint), [[basteln]] (do crafts), [[Musik hören]], [[am Computer spielen]], [[Karten spielen]].
Going out: [[essen gehen]], [[ins Kino gehen]], [[ins Fitnessstudio gehen]] (go to the gym), [[einkaufen]], [[tanzen]].
As a hobby a single verb becomes a noun with a capital letter: [[Mein Hobby ist Kochen.]] A phrase like [[Musik hören]] usually stays as it is: [[Meine Hobbys sind Lesen und Musik hören.]]

phrases.de: Meine Hobbys sind Lesen und Musik hören.
phrases.en: My hobbies are reading and listening to music.

points: [[der Sport]] is sport; a kind of sport is [[die Sportart]].
Ball games: [[Fußball]] (ß sounds like ss), [[Basketball]], [[Tennis]], [[Tischtennis]] (table tennis), [[Golf]], American Football.
Others: [[Schwimmen]] (sch sounds like sh), [[Radfahren]] (cycling), [[Boxen]], [[Gymnastik]], [[Surfen]], [[Eiskunstlauf]] (figure skating), [[Autorennen]] (motor racing), [[Yoga]].
Long words are easier in parts: Tisch-tennis, Eis-kunst-lauf.

sections.title: Two ways to like
sections.text:
- [[mögen]] + a thing: [[Ich mag Kaffee.]] [[Ich mag den Film.]] (the accusative from lesson 2)
- a verb + [[gern]]: [[Ich trinke gern Kaffee.]] [[Ich schwimme gern.]] = I like swimming.

You met [[gern]] in Unit 1: [[Ich lerne gern Deutsch.]] It comes after the verb. With [[mögen]] you like a thing; with [[gern]] you like doing something.

Not liking: [[Ich mag keinen Fisch.]] [[Ich schwimme nicht gern.]]

sections.title: mag or möchte?
sections.text: [[Ich mag Kaffee.]] = I like coffee (in general). [[Ich möchte einen Kaffee.]] = I'd like a coffee (now, please). So order with [[möchte]], never with [[mag]].

sections.title: gern, lieber, am liebsten
rows: Most of all I like (drinking) water.

sections.text: [[lieber]] (more gladly) and [[am liebsten]] (most gladly) are the 'more' and 'most' of [[gern]]. They sit where [[gern]] sits: after the verb, or [[am liebsten]] first with the verb second. Other comparisons (bigger, the biggest) come at A2.

Russian люблю and Armenian սիրում եմ cover both: я люблю кофе, я люблю плавать. German splits them: [[Ich mag Kaffee.]] but [[Ich schwimme gern.]] And [[lieben]] is mostly for people: [[Ich liebe dich.]] For coffee, [[mögen]] or [[gern]] is the everyday choice.

sections.title: Does it taste good?
sections.text:
[[Das schmeckt gut!]] = That tastes good. [[Schmeckt's?]] = Do you like it? (said about food).

[[Es schmeckt mir.]] = I like the taste. [[mir]] is the chunk you know from [[Tut mir leid]]; Unit 6 explains it. And the one-word compliment you'll hear everywhere: [[Lecker!]] = Yummy!

sections.title: How often?
sections.text:
[[immer]] (always), [[oft]] (often), [[manchmal]] (sometimes), [[nie]] (never). They come after the verb, or first with the verb second:
- [[Ich koche oft.]]
- [[Ich trinke nie Kaffee.]]
- [[Manchmal koche ich am Abend.]]

To ask about hobbies: [[Was machst du gern?]] or [[Was ist dein Hobby?]] Munich is close to the Alps, so expect [[Ich wandere gern.]] a lot.

items.de: Was machst du gern? - Ich lese gern und ich wandere gern.
items.en: What do you like doing? - I like reading and hiking.

items.de: Magst du Fisch? - Nein, ich mag keinen Fisch.
items.en: Do you like fish? - No, I don't like fish.

items.de: Ich trinke gern Tee, aber am liebsten trinke ich Kaffee.
items.en: I like tea, but most of all I like coffee.

items.de: Am Wochenende mache ich oft Sport.
items.en: At the weekend I often do sport.
Most of all I like water.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I like coffee.
items.explanation: mögen + a thing: ich mag, with no ending.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I like swimming.
items.explanation: verb + gern = to like doing it. gerne is the same word.

items.question: Which sentence means 'I prefer tea'?
items.explanation: lieber = more gladly, so 'prefer'. gern = like, nie = never.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Do you like fish? (informal)
items.explanation: du magst. In a yes/no question the verb comes first.
oft comes after the verb, or first with the verb second.
